text: Author: Danny Newman July 2024 Airconditioner FJ Van sizing recommendation The above are the Dometic recommendations for the Freshjet range relative to RV size; It is important to note that this range are all inverter equipped so adjust compressor speed to suit the conditions. So, if the airconditioner is smaller in a bigger RV, it will adjust the speed upwards to meet the conditions so will run at a higher speed and therefore current draw to achieve the desired result. (If it can) With an airconditioner that is bigger than needed for the RV, it will adjust the compressor running speed downwards and only consume what it needs to meet the desired result. (And it can) Older style “on and off” cycling airconditioners, if you had one that was too big for the installation, you would see “short cycling” meaning lots of on and off clunking compressor noise and poor performance. It is hard to get it wrong with these units which are very efficient, but ensure you take into account things such as campers with canvas sides. Better to go bigger if you can as you are trying to air condition a tent with little insulative qualities in effect. Also consider the size and number of windows in any vehicle as heat ingress to the RV also has an effect, as does less than adequate insulation in the RV walls.

Airconditioner – Generator appropriate size and type selection These appliances are designed to run from AC mains, but customers will also want to use generators. There is often confusion in the RV industry not only from consumers, but sometimes from dealer staff when it comes to understanding what generator is needed to run the RV airconditioner. i.e. Just because an airconditioner is rated as a “3000-Watt unit”, that does not mean that you need a 3Kva generator to run the airconditioner. The 3000 watts is related to the heating or cooling output of the airconditioner. You only need the power that the airconditioner consumes in creating the cooling or heating output, and this is always less than the output capacity of the airconditioner, and we call that the required input wattage for our purposes. Generators Broad explanation: kVA = Kilo-Volt-Amperes kW = Kilowatts In a 100% efficient system kW would equal kVA. Most generators will have a power factor of 0.8 kW. (In effect this means 80% efficiency) That means that a 2kVA generator may only be putting out 1600 watts (1.6kW) of actual or usable power. In that above scenario - if the required maximum power usage (input wattage required) of an airconditioner is 1600 watts or less, then that 2kVA generator will run the airconditioner, if only the airconditioner is running from that generator. If multiple electric appliances are running from the same circuit, the power consumption of these also needs to become part of the equation. Output from the generator also needs to be stable, and with generators running electronic goods, it is important that the generator AC output is pure sine wave. Modern RV airconditioners are inverter equipped, which in broad terms means that the compressor speeds up and slows down rather than the older style airconditioner with which the compressor stopped and started. Dometic recommend only using modern pure sine wave equipped generators of suitable capacity to run our inverter airconditioners. If an older technology generator is used, when the airconditioner compressor slows down, the generator also may reduce output and cause the air-conditioner to go into an alarm condition if it senses undervoltage.

text: 1. Fabric stitching leaking This can be solved by applying a seam sealer to the fabric stitching. Even some brand-new fabrics could allow water through the stitch holes in the right conditions. Normally a few days in the sun causes the fabric to seal to the stiches, bu t seam sealer is available for stubborn cases. We suggest Gear Aid Seam Grip WP 2. Dent in roller tube Careless handling or a simple mishap can cause small dents in the roller tube. Customers generally do not like this of course. It is not necessary in a lot of cases to replace the tube to remove this cosmetic issue, simply remove the fabric from the roller tube sail track, turn the roller 1/3 and then reinsert the fabric to the sail track. The dent is no longer visible and as Danny used to say, “what the eye does not see the heart will not grieve”! 3. Rippling of the fabric or small delamination spots. Also, a cosmetic issue and does not stop the awning from doing what it is designed to do. Some small imperfections could be considered normal – this is basically a piece of vinyl after all. More severe cases may need warranty exchange. Some customers are more sensitive than others. Things like bird or bat poop left on an awning in the sun may cause some spotting. Cleaning after a trip is recommended. 4. Storm damage. It is recommended in the manual that awnings are rolled in during heavy or prolonged wind or rain. Storm damage is not covered by warranty. The product is designed specifically as an awning, rather than an Annex roof; if being used as an Annex roof, the customer is unlikely to roll the awning in when the wind picks up, so they need to be advised to have a proper slope on the awning so that a dam of rainwater cannot build up on the awning, and secure it with guy ropes to prevent the wind turning ripping it off the RV. The Dometic recommendation is that the awning is rolled in for stormy weather. 5. Usage damage. Rolling the awning up wet or applying chemicals when cleaning can cause cosmetic damage to the fabric. Recommend drying the awning prior to rolling up and only using warm soapy water to clean the awning then let it dry in the sun. ISSUES YOU MAY SEE

text: UNDERSTANDING DEFROST Combined Defrost And Low Ambient Control Heaters. The display PCB operates the defrost and low ambient heaters. Two 10-watt heaters connected in parallel are used to heat the cooling plate and surrounding air in the fresh food compartment. UNDERSTANDING LAC (LOW AMBIENT CONDITION) The LAC function is switched on when the NTC in the fresh food compartment has been off for more than 35 minutes. The LAC heater remains operational in 5 second on and 5 second off cycles and the cooling unit switches on to maintain freezer temperature. When the temperature in the fresh food compartment reaches the cut in level, the heater is switched off, and the cooling unit continues to run. * The reason for LAC is so that the freezer remains cold enough in cold climates when the fresh food compartment is not working hard. The freezer is a “slave” to the refrigerator in effect. Forced Defrost the forced defrost function is activated if the system has been running for 30 hours without cycling, this defrost is terminated when NTC1 sense the plate temperature at 3 degrees above normal cut in temperature for the setting being used. Heaters operate at full power. Normal Defrost – Heater Does Not Come On At All System cycles while fan maintains air circulation around the cooling plate.

text: NO POWER - CLIXON If the refrigerator has an adequate DC supply at the house battery input on the terminal block, but there is no power reaching the Display PCB or Main PCB, the fault is likely related to the Clixon thermal switch. In rare cases, the issue may be caused by a failed thermal fuse. What is a Clixon? A Clixon is a thermal safety switch designed to protect an appliance from overheating or excessive electrical current. The Clixon fitted to RUA refrigerator flue is equipped with a manual reset button, allowing the switch to be reset once the cause of the over-temperature condition has been identified and corrected. text: BATTERY CONFIGURATION Series Connecting four 12 V 100 Ah batteries in series increases the battery bank voltage to 48 V while maintaining the available capacity at 100 Ah. This is achieved by connecting the positive terminal of each battery to the negative terminal of the next battery, causing the individual battery voltages to add together. In a series battery bank, the maximum current output at any given moment is limited to the rating of a single battery because the same current must flow through every battery in the series string. Increasing the number of batteries in series increases voltage, but it does not increase the maximum current capability. Parallel Connecting four 12 V 100 Ah batteries in parallel keeps the battery bank voltage at 12 V while increasing the available capacity to 400 Ah. This is achieved by connecting all positive terminals together and all negative terminals together. In a parallel battery bank, the maximum current output at any given moment increases because each battery shares the load. The total current capability is the sum of the current capability of all batteries connected in parallel. Parallel Series (4800 W) (4800 W)

text: INVERTOR TECHNOLOGY Did you know: The Dometic Harrier Inverter was introduced in late 2016 and is widely recognized as the first rooftop reverse-cycle air conditioner to use an inverter compressor in an RV An invertor compressor uses variable speed technology to continuously adjust cooling or heating output, rather than repeatedly switching completely on and off like older fixed- speed units. Benefits include: • More efficient performance across a wide temperature range. • Quieter operation with no “on and off” clunks caused by “torque bite”. • An optimal speed is automatically selected; the compressor adjusts running speed as required. It is possible for non-inverter models to be too big for an installation, which can lead to short cycling and associated problems, with these, even though the capacity may be bigger than needed for some RV, only the capacity that the vehicle requires is used.

text: MAINTENANCE TASKS Poor upkeep of an air -conditioning unit will increase power usage, reduce performance and increase likelihood of future repairs. Maintenance becomes even more important if the RV has been used in dirty and dusty locations for extended periods. Maintenance Checklist 1. Clean Filters regularly . 2. Clear rooftop grill/fans of any debris or obstructions such as sticks, leaves and nests. 3. Clear condensate drain holes of any debris or obstructions, If a drain pan kit is fitted, verify that condensation water flows freely through the drain system. 4. Clean evaporator and condenser coil with a brush, low pressure compressed air and non- corrosive enzyme type coil cleaner . 5. Straighten any bent fins on evaporator and condenser coils with fin comb. 6. Ensure all components are operating correctly . An air ON/OFF performance test is recommended. The expected temperature differential (split) is 12° C to 16° C, although this may vary depending on ambient temperature and compressor speed at the time of testing. 7. Ensure all four securing bolts are correctly tensioned to 2.5 – 4 Nm of torque.

text: DC wiring to Refrigerator Wiring needs to be sufficiently heavy to carry the load. The thinner the incoming wiring to the refrigerator, the greater the voltage loss. The longer the run of wiring from the battery to the refrigerator, the greater the voltage loss. All joins/connections along the run are potential voltage loss areas. Under load, that is as the compressor starts, the voltage loss is increased substantially; without load, that is when the compressor is not running, you will be able to measure what appears to be suitable voltage to enable the refrigerator to run. The refrigerator compressor can try to start, which causes a voltage loss due to inadequate wiring and the compressor shuts down and a one flash error appears. Immediately the compressor stops, the load is no longer there, so the voltage once again shows higher, and the compressor tries to start again and once again shuts down as the voltage drops. (Over and over) Don’t be fooled, always measure the available voltage under load conditions. Below table is a good guide for wiring to compressor refrigerators. Solar and battery storage When fitting a solar electrical system, it is important to know what is the likely power drain from the battery storage every day; add up all of the consumers and a good rule of thumb is to try to have around 2/3 in storage. Example: You expect to consume 100 amphours each day in total, good practice would be to have 300 Amphours of battery storage capacity; this helps with cloudy days limiting solar input. It is always better to have more than you need. What size solar? With the “electrification” of the industry, much bigger and more elaborate systems are being fitted. For a basic system, a rough guide/formula to refer could be: Solar Panel watts, divided by DC voltage, multiplied by 5 sunlight hours per day. SO: 120-Watt panel on a 12 volts system equals 10. 10 multiplied by 5 good sunlight hours equals 50. Potential provision around 50 Amphours per day. So, if you needed 100 Amphours per day, you would need at least 2 X 120-Watt panels, and it would be better to have more if you have the real estate on the roof of the RV. Personal opinion, If I want 100 amphours per day, I am going to fit 300 watts of solar panel & 300 Amphours of battery. I would go Lithium also as it charges more quickly and holds a higher voltage for longer than AGM/Deep cycle batteries. Make sure the charger and regulator are MPPT suitable for Lithium. text: RCD control panel modes. Performance mode uses automatic compressor speed, automatic outer fan and automatic defrost at cooling levels 1-5 and is the preferred general mode. Silent mode limits compressor speed, keeps the outer fan low, uses automatic defrost and levels 1-3; high ambient temperatures may cause long run times and reduced performance. Turbo uses high compressor and fan speed, disables defrost, selects coldest level 5 and runs for at most 12 hours before reverting. Low Ambient Condition uses a 5 W heater below 12 C to prevent freezer warming while the fresh-food section waits to restart.

text: RCD Low Ambient Control heater operation: one temperature sensor in the refrigerator section controls the compressor, so in cold weather the freezer can warm while the refrigerator remains cold enough not to call for cooling. When the compressor cycles off and the LAC sensor detects ambient below 12 C, the 5 W heater switches on to warm the fresh-food evaporator and force an earlier compressor restart. The heater switches off when the compressor starts. This repeats until the sensor detects 15 C. The heater remains off during a refrigerator-stopping fault such as compressor low-voltage cut-out.

text: RCD warning and error alarms: solid warning means defective fresh-food sensor and sensor replacement is required. One flash means DC below 10 V or above 31.5 V; check wiring, connections, battery condition and connected solar, inverter or adaptor equipment. Two flashes means external-fan overcurrent; reset with the power button for 2 seconds and replace the fan if repeated. Three flashes means compressor will not start; check power interruptions, control module, refrigerant overcharge or locked rotor. Four flashes means compressor overload; reset, switch off 30 minutes and reduce load. Five flashes means compressor overheat; check ventilation and fan. Six flashes means CI-BUS fault and auto-resets. Seven flashes means door open more than 2 minutes and resets when closed.

text: Author: Danny Newman November 2024 RCD10.5XS power consumption This document is designed to remove confusion as to what power you can expect to consume running on 12 volts with the RCD10.5XS upright two door compressor fridge – freezer. Rated power: 9.5 Amps In the case of the RCD10.5XS this should be seen as the maximum power that the refrigerator will consume from the battery at any moment. The highest power consumption occurs at start up when the refrigerator is warm, but once down to temperature the refrigerator compressor will consume less power. As this above figure is shown in Dometic official documentation – people may think that that is an average hourly consumption figure, but it is not. The average consumption figure is much lower. What is important to know and understand: The average hourly power consumption over a 24-hour period. Understanding this allows one to size their battery and solar appropriately so that the refrigerator does not run out of power/flatten the batteries. The average consumption can vary with the ambient temperature; at an ambient of 30 Celsius, the refrigerator needs to consume more power than when the ambient is 25 Celsius. There are also other variables such as wiring size impacting on voltage loss, humidity, stock in the refrigerator, how often and how long the door is opened, how cold it is set and so on. Due to vacuum panel assisted insulation and other considerations such as size of the condenser in this model, these are very efficient refrigerators and the cycle on times are relatively short, so when the compressor is cycled off as the refrigerator is cold enough, there is virtually no power consumption at all – just milliamps to power the electronics. (Let’s call it “standby” consumption – same as your TV at home when off.) It is not feasible for a manufacturer to provide precise consumption figures for all variable situations, but below information will help determine what is needed. From Dometic production plant testing on RCD10.5XS: With an ambient temperature of 27C, with the temperature setting on setting 3, with a full battery at 13.29 volts, the refrigerator will consume 1.8 amphours per hour on average whilst those conditions remain. That means in the unlikely event that the ambient temperature did not change from 27C for 24 hours – the refrigerator would consume 24 X 1.8amps = 43.2 amphours from the battery for that day. If the Ambient was 32C for the daylight 12 hours and 22C for the night 12 hours, that means the average temperature for that day was 27C so – dependent still on other variables - the refrigerator should have consumed around 45 amphours from the battery storage for that day. Tip; As all refrigerators need to run more in hot climates – it pays to allow a little extra. Ensure that you have enough for pretty much all Australian areas by assuming 2.3 – 2.5 amps per hour, size your batteries and solar array accordingly, and you are unlikely to run out of power due to the refrigerator consuming too much.
